Only 22% of remote USD jobs list a pay figure. The rest are marked DOE—determined on experience. What does that mean for your salary negotiation?

Our analysis of 4,280 active remote listings on Loker Dollar found:
• 940 listings (22%) disclose a concrete USD salary
• 3,340 listings (78%) leave pay blank, signaling DOE
• 64% (2,735) accept applicants from any country
• 1,213 listings were posted in the last 7 days

Example: Online Consumer Panels America offers $25–$45/hour for product assessments. But most roles, like Senior HR Generalist at Pearster, don't show a range.

DOE isn't necessarily a red flag. It can be a negotiation lever. Companies use it to attract broader talent and tailor pay to seniority. In specialized fields like AI or healthcare, top candidates can push salaries above market averages.

How to negotiate a DOE wage:
1. Research global benchmarks
2. Quantify your impact with metrics
3. Anchor with a range at the high end
4. Ask about total compensation
5. Reference industry trends
